main_text.p: missionibus & minis Dei, & gratuito fœdere in Christo symbolísque eius complectitur: & Patrum exempla historiásque narrans dogmata quoque & sensum fidei cultúmque religionis illorum explicat. Quid? nónne fundamenta omnia gratiæ & fœderis diuini ex libro Genesᵉos maxime à Paulo petuntur passim? vt Rom.4.Galat.3.& 4.&c.

14.Ibid. Quomodo iustificarentur homines tempore Adæ, Henoch, Noë.] Negatur. hoc enim Deus tradiderat Gen. 3. & ipse Adam aliíque Patres prædicatione fidei, sacrificiis, & toto cultu religiose professi sunt.

15.Art.18. Per illud, officiu, intelligere non solum lachrymas, sed etiam orationem & ieiunium?] quis prohibeat intelligere, nisi Hebræa veritas? nihil enim amplius dicit Moses, quàm à conspectu mortui sui, siue à præsentia, quemadmodum & Ixx. Augustino teste, ... Interpretatio illa vulgata abest à verbis Mosis longissimè. quid inde probes?

16.Ibid. Cupierunt ossa sua deferri in terram promissionis, nisi quia ibi solum sacrificia pro defunctis facienda esse noverant?] Non propterea cupiuerunt: sed tribus de causis cupiuerunt, quarum prima ciuilis est, & duæ religiosæ. Ciuile est, mortuos, viros, præsertim magnos, in patriam suam & sepulchreta familiarica sua exportari: quod vsus communis docet. Causa religiosa est vna, vt sancti illi patres docerent fratres & posteros suos fidem suam hoc symbolo moribundi, & in eadem fide ipsos informarent: altera, vt eadem occasione etiā religiose obstringeret eos exemplo fidei, & præcepto vltimæ voluntatis, & religione iuramenti. vide Genef. 48.7. & 21. & 49. 29. & 50.24. & sequentibus.

page.notes: The Hebrew and Greek fragments (the Greek word after "Augustino teste," and the Hebrew-letter quotation) are printed in their scripts but are too faint to read reliably; they are marked with "..." above, which should be replaced by a [illegible, ~N letters] marker if the script requires it. The Greek phrase after "Augustino teste," reads approximately "τὰ πεχρὰ αὐτῶν" but is not certain. The word "Genesᵉos" is a doubtful reading of "Geneseos". The "17. Art." at the foot is treated as a catchword, but it may be a signature-like line; the heading-style number 17 is not a section head. Side notes: the numbers 14, 15, 16 are in the left margin and are the only marginal text.
